140: - Problem: direct plugin installs accept `http://`, `git://`, and `file://` remotes, and marketplace add accepts `http://...git`, with no warning or policy knob. Marketplace entries may pin SHA, but direct source parsing has no immutable pin concept.
141: - Impact: users can install executable plugin code over unauthenticated transports, making MITM or local path confusion part of the plugin trust surface.
142: - Concrete fix: default to `https`/SSH only, require an explicit unsafe flag for `http://` and `git://`, and encourage or require full SHA pins for remote plugin installs where possible.

144: ### 11. `copy-assets.mjs` silently succeeds when a glob matches zero files
145: 
146: - File: `scripts/copy-assets.mjs:43`
147: - File: `scripts/copy-assets.mjs:49`
148: - File: `scripts/copy-assets.mjs:54`
149: - File: `packages/core/package.json:24`
150: - File: `packages/core/package.json:25`
151: - Problem: for glob inputs, `copy-assets.mjs` only checks that the source directory exists. If `src/prompt/sections/*.md` or `src/data/*.json` accidentally matches zero files, the build succeeds with missing runtime prompt/data assets.
152: - Impact: packaging can ship a broken or reduced prompt/data bundle without an early failure.
153: - Concrete fix: track matches per glob and exit non-zero when a glob argument matches zero files, unless a future caller explicitly marks the pattern optional.
